Home Department No. 1 of 1855 - Narrative of the proceedings of the Government of the Straits of Malacca for the first quarter of 1855, prepared by E A Blundell, Governor of the Straits Settlements. Issues covered for the quarter include: 1) decision on duties on wild and cultivated nutmegs; 2) inquiry into the death of a Prussian supposedly killed during the May Riot in Singapore; 3) private memorial to the Government seeking redress from Siamese authorities; 4) personnel matters concerning appointments, salaries, pensions, leave applications and duties of various civil servants; 5) returns of sugar and rum manufactured in Penang and Province Wellesley; 6) discussion on the Law of Inheritance, the Draft Act for preservation of the Public Peace, and Excise Act 14 of 1851; 7) education matters concerning the Malacca Free School, Singapore Institution Free School, and state of education in the Straits; 8) raising of the patriotic fund in Singapore; 9) various convict matters, including classification, pensions, entitlements and treatment; 10) discussion on marketability of pineapple hemp and plumbags; 11) resignation of Col. Butterworth as Governor and new appointments made thereafter; 12) supply of coal to Penang depot; 13) table of fees for the Admiralty Court; 14) legal cases concerning recovery of fines and payment; and 15) complaints regarding the new postal arrangements in Singapore.
